audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers give Kayle levels 2 and 3 and call level 6 'Skill', while the prose in the same file says the opposite: whys[0] and whys[1] describe Nautilus winning outright, whys[2] calls level 3 a coin-flip, and whys[4] says level 6 is where she becomes a kiter he cannot catch.
audit.why: Packet levelChart reads Nautilus / Nautilus / Skill / Skill / Kayle / Kayle / Kayle, which matches the written whys and the kit: Kayle is melee with no dash until 6 against a hook-plus-root opener.
audit.corrected: Row 0 -> Nautilus, row 1 -> Nautilus, row 2 -> Skill, row 4 -> Kayle; rows 3, 5, 6 unchanged. Full and content flipped in matched pairs.

audit.why: Four spikes present and correctly sited: Nautilus levels 1-3, Kayle at 6 (Divine Ascent ranged + Divine Judgment), Kayle first item (Nashor's), Kayle late (level 16 ranged AoE).

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown is stated anywhere despite Dredge Line being the whole matchup, and the terrain behaviour of the hook is never mentioned. Kayle has no dash at any point in her kit.
audit.why: Dredge Line is 14/13/12/11/10s, Riptide 7/6.5/6/5.5/5s, Depth Charge 120/100/80s. Riot's text also states that colliding with terrain pulls Nautilus toward it, so a wall behind you is a gap-close, not cover — and with no dash, Flash is the only answer.
audit.corrected: State the 14s rank-1 hook window as the trade trigger, the 5-7s Riptide, and hold Flash for the hook rather than for the damage.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect: no cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere — every line says 'when Dredge Line is down' without a number.
audit.why: A 14-second rank-1 hook is a long, concrete window; naming it turns vague advice into a countable one.
audit.corrected: Numbers added to breakdown.cooldowns and phases[1].why.

edits.before: You are the weakest level 1 in the game — pay rent quietly. Identify how Nautilus contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Weakest level 1 in the game — pay rent quietly. Stay off the hook angle: Staggering Blow roots on his first auto and Riptide finishes it.

edits.before: E-poke softens his step-ups while you scale. Only take the trade when Nautilus's Dredge Line is down.
edits.after: Dredge Line is 14s at rank 1; while it is up his hook-root all-in beats you. Trade only after he whiffs it.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Nautilus must walk into your range.
edits.after: Radiant Blast's resist shred starts to bite, but one landed hook still flips any trade — a coin-flip settled at max range.

edits.before: Level 6 / 11 / 16 are the actual matchups — everything before is stalling. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Nautilus's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Divine Ascent goes ranged and Divine Judgment blanks his Depth Charge knockup — pop R on the hook-into-R and you kite a man who cannot reach you.

edits.before: - Nautilus Dredge Line: matchup-defining — His only engage. Dodge it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Nautilus Dredge Line: matchup-defining — 14/13/12/11/10s and his only engage. Dodge it, then step up. - Riptide: 5-7s, never stand in the pulses. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.

edits.before: Survive Nautilus's Q-hook-into-passive-root all-ins through levels 1-5 without dying or flashing
edits.after: Survive his hook-root all-ins through 1-5 — you have no dash, so hold Flash for the hook, not the damage

notes: suspectNames flagged "Divine Judgment's" in wants.you[1] — false positive, correct name for Kayle's R. The kit's derived 'terrain' flag on Dredge Line reads 'creates terrain, blocks paths and dashes', which contradicts Riot's description (colliding with terrain pulls Nautilus toward it). Followed the description: the hook is a gap-close off walls, not a wall itself.
